transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess I’ve just been feeling kind of low for a long time. I still get through my routes and I do my volunteer shifts and all that, so it’s not like I’m falling apart or anything… but most days there’s this heavy feeling on me. Like I’m just going through the motions instead of really being in my own life, if that makes sense.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Um… I’d say it’s been about three years now. It kind of started after my father died. I mean, I’ve been managing okay, but that’s when I first really noticed it hanging around.
Have you ever experienced times when your mood was unusually high or elevated, where you felt more energetic, more confident, or even irritable for a period of time?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I have good days here and there, or times I’m a little more upbeat if something goes right, but nothing where I’d say I felt unusually high or out of control or anything like that. At least not that I’ve noticed… is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that activities you once found pleasurable now feel flat or uninteresting?

I’m not sure… I mean, I still do things, so I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Some things maybe don’t feel as satisfying, but I can’t tell if that’s just getting older or being tired. I wouldn’t say everything is flat, exactly. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Can you think of a time when you used to really enjoy something, like a hobby or spending time with friends, and now it just doesn't feel the same or feel enjoyable anymore?

I’m trying to think… I don’t know if there’s one clear thing like that. I still see people sometimes, still do normal stuff when I can. Maybe it doesn’t always feel as fun as I think it should, but I wouldn’t want to say I don’t enjoy it anymore. Maybe I just get worn out easier or expect less, I guess. Does that answer it okay?
Is there a difference in how much pleasure or enjoyment you get out of activities now compared to before you started feeling this way, even if you still do them?

I’m not totally sure how to measure it. I guess maybe some things don’t hit the same way they used to, but I still can enjoy stuff sometimes, so I wouldn’t want to overstate it. It’s more like… maybe it’s a little muted now and then, but not gone. Does that make sense?

Can you think of something that used to be enjoyable for you, maybe even just a small thing like a TV show, a hobby, or time with someone close, where now it just doesn’t feel the same or you don’t get as much out of it?

I’m honestly having a hard time coming up with a specific example. I mean, I watch shows or spend time with people and sometimes I’m maybe not as into it as I used to be, but I can’t say there’s one thing that’s clearly just… not enjoyable anymore. It might just depend on the day. I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. Is that still helpful?
Can you think of a specific activity or something you used to enjoy, even a small thing, where now it just doesn’t feel as good or you don’t look forward to it anymore?

I’m sorry, I’m still kind of blanking on a specific one. I don’t think there’s anything I can point to and say, “I used to love that and now I don’t.” Some days I might not look forward to things as much, but once I’m doing them, they can still be okay. I don’t want to give you a bad example just to have an answer. Does that make sense?
Can you describe how your mood typically is by the end of the day? Is it something that's consistently low or heavy, or does it tend to vary a lot depending on what happened that day?

By the end of the day it’s usually… I don’t know, kind of heavy, I guess. Not every single minute depends on something bad happening, it’s more like it’s sitting there most days. I still get through my routes and I do my volunteer shifts, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart or anything. But a lot of the time it feels like I’m just going through the motions instead of really feeling like I’m in my own life. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find that most days, for most of the day, your mood is consistently low or heavy, even if it doesn’t always feel the same throughout the day?

Yeah… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because I still do my routes and I show up for my volunteer shifts, but most days there’s this low, heavy feeling kind of sitting on me. It may shift a little during the day, but it’s usually there, like I’m just getting through things rather than really feeling present in my life.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels, or do you ever feel like you're not good enough or blame yourself for things more often than before?

Sleep, maybe, yeah. I don’t want to overstate it because I still get up and make it to work on time, but on nights before a run I’ll lie there thinking about the next day’s stops. Or I’ll wake up around four and then I don’t really get back to sleep. So I can function, but I start the day already kind of worn down, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed that you feel more down on yourself lately, like you're not good enough or that you're failing more often than you should, even if it's not necessarily tied to a specific event?

Yeah… I guess I do, more than I like to admit. It’s not like anyone’s telling me I’m failing or anything. People are mostly fine with me. But in my own head I keep comparing myself to the kind of man my dad was, and I feel like I should be further along by now, or handling things better than this. I don’t know if that’s what you mean, but… yeah, that voice is there.
Can you think of something you used to do that you really looked forward to, where now you don’t feel that same sense of anticipation or enjoyment, even if you still do it?

I’m not sure I can point to one thing exactly. I mean, I still do the things I’m supposed to do, and some things are okay once I’m there. Maybe I don’t get excited ahead of time the way I used to, but I don’t know if that’s just getting older or being tired, you know?

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Nothing comes to mind like, “I loved that and now I hate it.” It’s more… I guess I don’t look forward to much the same way. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Can you think of something you used to really enjoy, even just a small thing, where now it doesn’t feel as good or you don’t look forward to it anymore, even if you still do it?

I’m trying to think of a good example, but honestly nothing clear pops up. I don’t want to give you an answer just to sound like I’m being helpful.

There are little things that maybe don’t feel as… I don’t know, fun as they used to, but I’m not sure I’d say I used to really enjoy something and now I don’t. It’s more vague than that for me. If that’s okay to say.
Would you say that your mood is low or heavy for most days and for most of the day, even if it varies a little here and there?

Yeah… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because I still get through my routes and I still show up for my volunteer shifts and all that.

But most days there is this kind of heavy, low feeling sitting on me. It’s like I’m doing what I need to do, but I’m more just going through the motions than really being in my own life, if that makes sense. It varies some, but… yeah, it’s there a lot.
Would you say that your low or heavy mood has been present for most of the day, more days than not, for at least two years?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t love saying it that way, because it makes it sound like I’ve just been stuck, but if I’m being honest, it’s been about three years now.

It seemed to start after my father died. I kept thinking it would lift after a while, and some days are better than others, but that heavy feeling has been there more days than not since then. Does that sound like what you’re asking?
